# Test fixtures

Every fixture is either synthetic or a session of a public repo passed through `scripts/redact-fixture.mjs` and then checked by hand (spec section 9.7). Nothing comes from private folders, employer repos or private projects. The script is an allow-list: it keeps numbers, booleans, `null`, record timestamps, and string values only at the record paths the parsers read (record type and subtype, version, entrypoint, model id, roles, content block types, tool names, attachment type, hook event, instruction scope, compaction trigger). Inside tool inputs and tool results every string is redacted. Object keys are kept only from a fixed list of known schema keys (plus model ids, the keys of cost-state `modelUsage`). Ids and uuids are replaced by stable fake ids of the same shape (the same id maps to the same fake id in every file, also when it is an object key). Paths under the session's repo root become `/repo/...`. Read results are replaced by synthetic code with the same line count (`function fnN`). Every other string and key, including MCP server and tool names, hook names, skill names, user-level instruction files and their paths, becomes `x` repeated to the same length. `api-request-blob` and `api-request-shape` records, which the parsers skip, are dropped.

The three redacted Claude files were redacted first with the original key-based script, then passed again through the allow-list script (`--repo-root /repo --keep-branch --keep-ids`; the ids were already fake), so everything the first pass kept that the allow-list does not is now redacted too.

## Claude Code

**`claude/basic-2.1.316.jsonl`**: one complete, untrimmed headless session (Claude Code 2.1.316, `entrypoint: sdk-cli`) from the public why-diff repo's benchmark runs (`bench/runs/f03-business-days--baseline--r2`). Redacted with `--repo-root <that run's cwd> --keep-branch` (the branch is `main`). It has `Grep`, `Glob`, `Read`, `Edit` and `Bash` calls, `instructions`, `prompt_snapshot` (with and without `tools`), `deferred_tools_delta`, a `cost-state` (the file is untrimmed, so its total covers exactly the requests in it), 1h cache writes, and a response split over three lines with one `message.id`. Being headless, it has no `hook_success` or `skill_listing`; the compaction fixture covers those.

**`claude/compaction-subagent/`**: a session from a throwaway sandbox repo (`git init -b fixture-branch`, a 4-line synthetic `math.js` and a 2-line `CLAUDE.md`), Claude Code 2.1.316. It was not captured anew for this fixture: the sandbox session the project's architect had already recorded with the same steps as the plan (Task 2, step 1.3) was redacted instead. In it a general-purpose subagent reads `math.js`, the main agent writes `notes.txt`, reads the missing `README.md` (an error result), runs `ls`, edits `math.js`, then `/compact` (manual), then reads `math.js` again. The main file, the subagent file `subagents/agent-<id>.jsonl` and its `.meta.json` were redacted with `--repo-root <sandbox> --keep-branch`; the folder and file names use the fake ids the script maps (`--map-id`). The user-level `CLAUDE.md`, the hooks, the skill listing and the MCP tool names of the machine it was captured on survive only as same-length `x` strings. The subagent's Read result has no `toolUseResult`, which is how 2.1.316 writes subagent Reads.

**`claude/legacy-inline-sidechain.jsonl`**: hand-written, synthetic. The older layout (version `1.0.80`, `Task` tool) where subagent records sit inline in the session file with `isSidechain: true` and no `agentId`; the usage has no 5m/1h `cache_creation` split; ends with a `summary` record.

**`claude/mcp-and-image.jsonl`**: hand-written, synthetic (shapes of 2.1.316). A user prompt with a text block and a base64 `image` block, a `deferred_tools_delta` that surfaces `mcp__docs__search`, a call to that MCP tool and its result, a Read of `assets/logo.png` whose result is an `image` block with base64 data, a `Bash` `cat src/logo.ts`, an assistant record with `model: "<synthetic>"` and all-zero usage, and one record of an unknown type.

## Codex

All Codex fixtures are hand-written and synthetic. The only local Codex rollout belongs to a private project, so only its key structure informed these shapes (spec section 3.2); no line, path or text comes from it.

**`codex/rollout-0.162.jsonl`**: the CLI `0.162.0-alpha.17.2` shape (`timestamp`, `type`, `payload`, `ordinal`). A `session_meta` (cwd `/home/dev/shop`, branch `feat/cart`, `base_instructions`), `turn_context` with model `gpt-6-astra`, a developer message, the `# AGENTS.md instructions for /home/dev/shop` user message, an `<environment_context>` message, a user prompt with an `input_image`, three `token_usage_record`s (`input_tokens` includes `cached_input_tokens`), `exec` `custom_tool_call`s each followed by an `item_completed` `CommandExecution` (`parsed_cmd` of type `read` for `cat src/cart.ts` twice, `search` once) and the call output, an `apply_patch` with `*** Update File: src/cart.ts`, a `compacted` record followed by an `event_msg` `context_compacted`, an assistant message mentioning `applyDiscount`, and ignored `world_state`, `task_started` and `task_complete` records.

**`codex/rollout-legacy.jsonl`**: the older shape. A `session_meta`, a `function_call` `shell` with `{"command":["bash","-lc","cat src/a.ts"]}` and its JSON-wrapped output (`{"output": ..., "metadata": {"exit_code": 0}}`), and three `event_msg` `token_count` records whose `total_token_usage` increases, stays the same, then increases again; no `token_usage_record`.

## Second review round (tasks 4 to 6)

The three redacted Claude files were passed once more through the allow-list script (`--repo-root /repo --keep-branch --keep-ids`), which now maps every opaque id that is not a uuid or a vendor id even with `--keep-ids` (a hook's 12-character `toolUseID` was an original id) and keeps `message.usage.speed` and `message.usage.inference_geo`. The earlier passes had replaced those two values with `x` runs, so they were restored by length to the only documented values of that length, `standard` (8) and `global` (6); this is an inference, not the original value. The same fields inside an Agent `toolUseResult.usage`, which is never priced, stay redacted.

## Canary

**`claude/canary/`**: hand-written, synthetic (generated once by a throwaway script, shapes of 2.1.316), for the `--share` leak tests. Session `c0ffee00-9f30-4a11-8000-00000000ca9a` in `/home/canary-user/acme-repo` on branch `feat/CANARY-BRANCH-7`. Every free-text field carries its own marker `CANARY_<field>_9f3`: the user prompt, assistant text, Read paths (in the repo, under `/etc/CANARY_ABS/`, under the home directory) and their contents, a Bash command and its output, a Grep pattern and output, an MCP query and result, an Edit's strings and result, instruction file paths and contents, a skill listing, a system prompt and tool description, a hook name, output and command, a PR link and URL, the entrypoint, the compaction summary, `ai-title`, `last-prompt` and `summary` records, and a subagent (`subagents/agent-CANARY_AGENTID_9f3.jsonl`) with its type, description, prompt, answer and a read. Model ids, tool names and the MCP server name (`docs`) are kept by `--share` (spec 9.6), so they carry no marker.
